stories.title: India recovers 7 bodies swept downstream after Nepal floods
stories.summary: Indian authorities recovered seven bodies swept downstream from Nepal floods in Uttar Pradesh's Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts. The bodies are believed to be victims of Nepal's devastating flash floods, with efforts under way to identify them. The floods have killed nearly 500 people, with many still missing, highlighting the disaster's severe impact across Nepal, China, and India. LUCKNOW, India - The Indian authorities recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be victims of devastating floods, officials said on Aug 28, underscoring the scale of the deadly disaster. The bodies were found floating in rivers in the Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts of Uttar Pradesh state, which borders Nepal’s southern flood-hit Chitwan region. “Four unidentified bodies were recovered in the district on Thursday (Aug 27),” Maharajganj district magistrate Gaurav Singh Sogarwal told AFP news agency. “We think they have been swept into India from Nepal following flash floods there.” Three more bodies were recovered in Kushinagar district, around 70km downstream from the frontier, a police official confirmed. The authorities are working to identify the bodies.

stories.title: Tanker pays record $5.3m to transit Panama Canal amid El Niño drought
stories.summary: The US-built canal's main users are the United States, China, Japan, Chile and South Korea. A tanker carrying liquefied petroleum gas paid a record $5.3 million (€4.5 million) for priority passage through the Panama Canal ahead of El Niño-related restrictions, the waterway's deputy administrator told AFP on Thursday. South Korean company SK Gas paid the record sum for the G. Spirit to transit the canal on 1 September, two days before authorities are due to reduce the number of daily transits due to the El Niño weather phenomenon, Bloomberg reported. Panama declared an emergency over El Niño on Tuesday as a severe regional drought continues to deplete the water reserves needed to operate the canal. Rainfall deficits have reached up to 60% on the country's Pacific side, while 11 watersheds are already experiencing water stress. Central America is in the throes of a severe drought driven by El Niño, a weather pattern that warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, triggering worldwide changes in winds, atmospheric pressure and rainfall. Ships usually book their Panama Canal passage well in advance, while those without reservations face an average wait of five days. Last-minute slots can also be secured through an auction. The Panama Canal Authority said the average price paid at auction between October 2025 and February 2026 was around $55,000 (€47,000). In April, however, a vessel carrying liquefied natural gas paid $4 million (€3.4 million) to skip the queue and avoid delays as the war in the Middle East increased demand for moving vital cargo through the canal. The waterway, which handles around five percent of global maritime trade, will reduce daily transits from 36 to 34 from 3 September, before cutting them further to 32 later in the month.

stories.title: China halts rescues as glacier-dammed lake starts to overflow
stories.summary: Chinese authorities have mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys.
article_sentences: A glacier collapse on the China-Nepal border formed a debris-dammed lake that has started to overflow, forcing Chinese rescue teams to halt operations due to high flood risks.
The lake holds over 2.5 million cubic metres of water, with heavy rainfall forecast to add 3 million cubic metres, raising the risk of a catastrophic breach around Sept 1.
Nearly 1,000 people remain missing from the disaster, including 540 foreigners, while engineers work on drainage plans amid challenging terrain and unstable conditions.

A lake formed by debris from a glacier collapse that triggered catastrophic flooding on the China-Nepal border has begun to overflow, the Chinese authorities said on Aug 28, forcing rescue operations to be halted.
Nepal and China both warned on Aug 27 of fresh risks of flooding in the Himalayas, with a debris dam creating a lake upstream that has been threatening to collapse.
China has been racing to reduce the risk of more flooding at the disaster-stricken border crossing linking its Tibet region to Nepal, after hundreds were killed in a flash flood on Aug 26.

Risks of the lake bursting and potential secondary disasters such as mountain collapses and avalanches have prompted all Chinese rescue personnel and vehicles to withdraw to stand by in a safe area, state broadcaster CCTV said.

The lake’s reservoir has topped 2.5 million cubic metres of water, up from the estimated 1.5 million to 2 million cubic metres a Chinese eight-member engineering team dispatched to monitor the site recorded a day ago.
The Chinese authorities have mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the barrier lake, according to CCTV.
One of the engineers, Chen Hanxiao, said challenges included difficult access to the site.
“After the glacier collapse created the lake, many isolated cliffs and steep cliffs appeared along it,” Chen told CCTV on the evening of Aug 27.

Chen said the general approach to reducing the lake’s threat is to excavate a drainage channel at a lower point of the dam but the width and depth of that channel needed calculations based on how fast the water will flow and how quickly the lake will fill.
